title: Bittensor Daily News — October 29, 2026
summary: KR1 discloses 5,000 TAO and staking operations; SN75 Hippius documents a CDN firewall; SN68 NOVA develops a molecule-optimization agent with SN64 Chutes; SN1 Apex confirms URnetwork competition launch. Also: finalized SN8 burns, product/model updates and operator changes.

ecosystem.headline: KR1 discloses 5,000 TAO and launches Bittensor staking operations
ecosystem.summary: The October 29 issuer announcement says 5,000 TAO were acquired over recent months and staking operations have started. This is a listed-company allocation disclosure, not 5,000 TAO bought today. KR1 plans monthly unaudited holdings/income updates. Its forward reward estimate is variable; custody, individual purchases and customer demand were not independently traced.
ecosystem.ratingReason: A material issuer disclosure with timing and reward limitations explicit.

ecosystem.headline: Shizzy with TAO Templar today; Leadpoet remains rescheduled
ecosystem.summary: Today’s TAO Templar interview is scheduled October 29 at 1 PM ET/10 AM PT. Leadpoet with Gavin is November 5 at 11 AM ET/8 AM PT, not today. The October 27 Yanez interview remains a completed replay. The channel also added an October 28 members video; upcoming streams are separate from completed episodes.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Original Shizzy coverage with schedules and access status separated.

updates.headline: SN1 Apex: URnetwork latency competition confirmed live
updates.summary: Apex’s October 29 13:35UTC original confirms the external URnetwork competition went live today. Participants submit a single Go-file patch; approved winners are intended to merge into URnetwork’s codebase and become the next epoch baseline. This confirms participation availability, not a measured production-speed improvement or customer count. The original includes an unresolved X-users placeholder, which is excluded here.
updates.ratingReason: A specific new participation route; realized network improvements remain unmeasured.

updates.headline: SN8 Vanta: finalized 999.989986185 alpha burn
updates.summary: Successful SubtensorModule.AlphaBurned at finalized block 9389396, extrinsic 10, event 169 on 2026-10-29T12:19:00.001000+00:00. Exact amount is 999989986185 raw units. This explicit transaction burn meets the 100-alpha per-event minimum; it excludes miner withholding, fees and recycling. The transaction establishes execution, not the off-chain revenue source.

updates.headline: SN8 Vanta reports rising monthly alpha-burn totals
updates.summary: Arrash’s October 28 post reports roughly $32 k/$50 k/$88 k for July–September and $225 k October-to-date; November $400 k+ is a question, not a forecast guarantee. The official dashboard reviewed overnight showed $226,289 and 27,460.43 alpha for October,31.0% of miner alpha actually emitted month-to-date. These team aggregates include all event sizes and price conversions, unlike our 100-alpha per-event archive; they are not TAO burns or audited cash revenue.
updates.ratingReason: An attributed operating aggregate with denominator, scope and forecast limits.

updates.headline: SN16 changes its registered name from end game to EG
updates.summary: Finalized block 9,389,870 records a successful SubnetIdentitySet for SN16. Storage immediately before/after changes end game to EG; registered owner and registration height remain unchanged. This is a verified identity-name update, not evidence of a subnet sale. Prior editions retain the historical names.

updates.headline: SN19 Blockmachine publishes a workload-price comparison
updates.summary: The October 29 team post says it was cheapest in 8 of 15 workload/volume tests using public list prices. Treat this as a scoped benchmark claim, not universal lowest cost: workload, resource sizing and current provider prices determine applicability. The underlying benchmark was not independently rerun.
updates.ratingReason: A useful comparison lead with methodology limits explicit.

updates.headline: SN22 Desearch shares a social-analytics example with explicit denominators
updates.summary: The October 29 example excludes reposts from engagement rates, deduplicates repeated posts across pages and excludes missing-view records from per-view calculations. This matters for builders comparing social results without silently treating missing views as zero. The example is a developer pattern, not a new measured customer deployment.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete data-quality workflow.

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes supports NOVA’s optimization-agent development
updates.summary: Chutes’s October 28 confirmation supports METANOVA’s developing Hit-to-Lead agent. METANOVA says domain-specific inference was integrated into Chutes TEEs for confidential research. This is an implementation collaboration with intended internal-program use; neither post establishes clinical results, independently audited confidentiality or new paying usage.

updates.headline: SN67 Harnyx announces OpenRouter rerank tools for miners
updates.summary: The October 29 team announcement says miners can call paid OpenRouter rerank models with their existing OpenRouter key. Reranking orders retrieved candidates before an llm_chat call, offering a more selective research workflow. The announcement and attached launch graphic were reviewed; independent execution, cost savings and quality gains were not tested.
updates.ratingReason: A specific miner workflow capability with clear access terms; measured benefits are unverified.

updates.headline: SN68 NOVA develops a Hit-to-Lead optimization agent
updates.summary: METANOVA’s October 28 announcement describes adapting a NOVA Blueprint winner’s algorithm for iterative small-molecule optimization, with Onepot chemical libraries and Chutes domain models in TEEs. The next step is integration into METANOVA’s own program. Predicted affinity and synthesis plans are not experimental efficacy or a launched external drug-discovery service.
updates.ratingReason: A specific research-to-tool development path; next-stage validation remains pending.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius adds a documented CDN web application firewall
updates.summary: October 29 documentation describes per-zone custom rules, rate limits, IP/country/ASN lists, log-only testing and version rollback. Standard is $5 per zone/month; Advanced $20, prorated while active, with blocked requests unbilled. This adds an operational security control. The team says filtering runs in attested confidential VMs; no independent penetration test or privacy audit was performed.
updates.ratingReason: A documented new infrastructure capability with concrete controls and pricing.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX plans competition pause and demand-led inference rewards
updates.summary: In its October 29 announcement, SN92 REAX says both competition tracks will pause after Friday October 30 crowning slots. Inference rewards will move toward customer demand step by step starting the following week, with advance announcements. Existing crownings retain three days at full share, taper to zero by day seven, then keep-alive. The team reports one organically acquired customer making 1.7 million requests in a week; this is a team claim, not verified retention, revenue or subnet-wide adoption. The transition is planned, not an already executed emission change.
updates.ratingReason: Actionable miner participation and reward-transition plans; customer and performance figures remain team-reported.
